required_for_acceleration_or_displacemen: total falling mass if rotor is internal
computability_rule.missing_data_policy: Do not estimate; record the missing input and proceed to the next paper.

proposed_drop_experiment.spin_description: clockwise viewed from south toward north

literature_records.citation: Hayasaka et al., Speculations in Science and Technology 20, 173 (1997), as summarized by Luo et al.
literature_records.configuration: Single free-fall gyroscope; differential spin senses; vertical spin axis.
literature_records.reported_result: Luo et al. report an approximately 10^-4 relative fall-acceleration difference for one spin sense.
literature_records.reason: The reviewed public source does not provide the complete falling assembly and fall interval needed for an accurate acceleration or displacement calculation.
literature_records.time_modulation: No public time-tagged series suitable for a 12-hour analysis was located.

literature_records.citation: J. Luo et al., Phys. Rev. D 65, 042005 (2002).
literature_records.configuration: Two side-by-side free-fall test masses in 12 m vacuum tubes; one 420 g steel rotor at 17,000 rpm and one nonrotating reference; vertical interferometric readout.
literature_records.reported_result: No vertical differential acceleration at the relative 2 x 10^-6 level; horizontal deviation was not a precision observable.
literature_records.reason: The spin axis and measured optical axis were vertical. The current cross-product law predicts a transverse force, so the measured vertical channel is exactly blind in the ideal geometry. Exact date and time are unavailable, so only the maximum transverse envelope is computed.

literature_records.citation: Z. B. Zhou et al., Phys. Rev. D 66, 022002 (2002).
literature_records.configuration: Improved double free-fall interferometer with the same 420 g, 55 mm x 32 mm steel rotor at 17,000 rpm; effective 9 m height and 1.0 s analysis interval.
literature_records.reported_result: Null vertical result at 1.6 x 10^-7; residuals included 1.6 Hz frame motion and approximately 0.1 micrometre rotor-frequency vibration.
literature_records.reason: The measured axis was vertical and the rotor spin axis was vertical; the model response is transverse. Exact timestamp is unavailable, so the reported values are maximum envelopes.

literature_records.citation: C. G. Shao et al., Commun. Theor. Phys. 39, 297-300 (2003).
literature_records.configuration: Theoretical long-distance free-fall trajectory analysis for a rotating ball and a nonrotating shell; 40 s fall interval.
literature_records.reported_result: The authors analyzed Earth-rotation trajectory curvature and reported an order 10^-9 cm orbit difference under their spin-spin model for a 40 s fall.
literature_records.reason: The public source does not state the rotating ball RPM, mass, or geometry required to evaluate the current K-Field law. Its published displacement belongs to a different model and is retained only as a source result.
literature_records.time_modulation: No approximately 12-hour experimental series was reported.

literature_records.citation: A. L. Dmitriev, E. M. Nikushchenko, and S. A. Bulgakova, arXiv:0907.2790 (2009).
literature_records.configuration: Closed falling container with two coaxial horizontal-axis rotors; maximum approximately 20,000 rpm.
literature_records.reported_result: Reported acceleration increase 10 +/- 2 cm/s^2; reported no dependence on N-S versus W-E orientation and no daily dependence.
literature_records.reason: The paper refers rotor and container characteristics to an earlier source and does not include the mass and geometry needed for a source-controlled K-Field acceleration or displacement.
literature_records.time_modulation: The authors explicitly state that daily dependence was not observed, but no time series or harmonic analysis is supplied.

literature_records.configuration: Horizontal-axis aviation rotor in an isolated falling container; 20-400 Hz, 30 mm path, approximately 40 ms readout.
literature_records.reported_result: Reported stochastic frequency dependence, with narrow extrema most apparent near 320 and 360 Hz and predominantly negative acceleration changes.
literature_records.reason: Known RPM and fall path are insufficient because the active rotor mass, rotor geometry, and total accelerated mass are not stated.
literature_records.time_modulation: Sampling every 0.5-1 minute followed rotor spin-down; no 12-hour analysis was reported.

literature_records.citation: F. T. Han et al., Chinese Physics Letters 34, 100701 (2017).
literature_records.configuration: Proposed concentric aluminum hollow cylinders spinning about the instrument x-axis, aligned vertically during a 3.5 s Beijing drop.
literature_records.reported_result: Concept and error budget; projected differential uncertainty 7.2 microGal. The article does not report a completed anomalous drop result.
literature_records.reason: All mass, geometry, RPM, and drop-duration inputs are public. The spin and sensitive axes are both vertical, so the current K-Field force is transverse and the published x-axis measurement is geometrically blind.
literature_records.time_modulation: A single 3.5 s drop does not test 12-hour modulation; repeated time-tagged drops would be required.

literature_records.citation: T. Y. Liu et al., Scientific Reports 6, 31632 (2016).
literature_records.configuration: Beijing drop-tower residual-acceleration characterization with single and double capsules; no spinning test mass.
literature_records.reported_result: Double-capsule residual acceleration better than 2 x 10^-4 g0; major ordinary terms included air drag, capsule rotation, and instrument recovery.
literature_records.reason: No rotating active mass is present, so no rotor K-Field acceleration or displacement can be computed.

literature_records.citation: J. Min et al., npj Microgravity 7, 25 (2021).
literature_records.configuration: Twenty three-axis drop-tower tests of a Taiji-1 inertial-sensor substitute; no rotating test mass.
literature_records.reported_result: Lowest residuals approximately 13 micro-g horizontally and 58 micro-g along the fall axis; an 87 micro-g switching transient was identified.
literature_records.reason: No rotating active mass is present. The study supplies an ordinary residual benchmark only.

literature_records.citation: T. J. Quinn and A. Picard, Nature 343, 732-735 (1990).
literature_records.configuration: Static precision weighing of a 330 g rotor spinning down from 8,000 rpm.
literature_records.reported_result: Apparent mass changes became insignificant after friction-couple and temperature corrections.
literature_records.reason: No free-flight interval exists, so lateral drop displacement is not defined.

literature_records.citation: I. L. Lorincz and M. Tajmar, arXiv:1506.02689 (2015).
literature_records.configuration: Static weighing with multiple rotor orientations; brass rotor mass 112 g; speeds to more than 25,000 rpm.
literature_records.reported_result: Precession and vibration artifacts identified; null relative mass change below 2.6 x 10^-6.
literature_records.reason: No free-fall trajectory is present and the reviewed source does not provide the complete rotor geometry required by this audit rule.

literature_records.citation: J. M. Nitschke and P. A. Wilmarth, Phys. Rev. Lett. 64, 2115-2116 (1990).
literature_records.configuration: Static weighing across spin directions to 22,000 rpm.
literature_records.reason: No drop trajectory or free-flight interval exists.

required_missing_fields: direct lateral trajectory or velocity data
oscillating_test_mass_search_result.note: Dmitriev 2011 recommends rotating or oscillating test bodies but reports rotor data, not a controlled oscillating-mass drop trajectory.
